name: Math Foundations
tagline: Every number has a shape. Every shape has a reason.
subject: Mathematics
description: A workshop where numbers have physical weight and equations are machines you build with your hands. Addition is stacking blocks. Fractions are cutting pies. Algebra is a balance scale. Maren runs the workshop — she hands you the pieces and lets you figure out how they fit. No worksheets. No timed tests. Just building things that work and understanding why they work.

domains.name: Numbers & Operations
concepts: Counting, place value, and number sense
Addition and subtraction — with physical metaphors
Multiplication as repeated addition, arrays, and groups
Division as sharing and grouping
Fractions — cutting things into equal parts
Decimals and their relationship to fractions
domains.mastery_signal: Can add, subtract, multiply, and divide with confidence. Can explain fractions and decimals using real-world examples.

domains.name: Patterns & Early Algebra
concepts: Recognizing patterns — visual, numerical, and repeating
Variables as mystery numbers — solving for the unknown
Equations as balance scales — both sides must equal
Order of operations — PEMDAS without memorization, through logic
Negative numbers — debt, temperature, elevation
domains.mastery_signal: Can identify patterns, solve simple equations, and explain why the balance scale metaphor works

domains.name: Geometry & Measurement
concepts: Shapes — triangles, rectangles, circles, their properties
Perimeter and area — measuring the outside and inside
Volume — how much fits inside a box
Angles — right angles, acute, obtuse, measuring with a protractor
Symmetry and transformations — flips, slides, turns
domains.mastery_signal: Can calculate area and perimeter, identify angles by type, and explain symmetry using real objects

domains.name: Data & Probability
concepts: Collecting and organizing data — tally marks, tables, surveys
Bar graphs and line graphs — reading and creating
Mean, median, mode — three ways to describe the middle
Probability basics — likely, unlikely, certain, impossible
Making predictions from data — what does the pattern tell us?
domains.mastery_signal: Can create a simple graph from data, calculate the mean of a small dataset, and make a reasonable prediction based on probability

real_world_application: Solve everyday math problems confidently. Count money, measure things, read graphs, and think logically about numbers.
